_readme: The highest UNGRADED values in Pokemon, from pricecharting.com.
Written by scripts/sync-raw-top.mjs from the pages sync-graded-top.mjs
already cached. NO NETWORK: see that script's header before adding one.
WHAT THE NUMBER IS. PriceCharting's Ungraded column: a price guide value
for a loose, ungraded copy, computed by their algorithm from completed
eBay sales and their own marketplace. It is NOT a marketplace's market
price, NOT a live listing and NOT an auction result, and no page may
describe it as any of those.
EVERY LANGUAGE, ON PURPOSE. PriceCharting's Pokemon catalogue is not split
by language, and this ranking is not either. Half the top 100 is Japanese.
The argument is in the header of scripts/build-top100.mjs.
A SNAPSHOT. `checked` is the day the crawl read these pages, borrowed from
data/top-graded.json because they are the same crawl. Every row carries
the url it came from and the page prints both.
NOTHING HERE IS PUBLISHABLE UNTIL verify-raw-top.mjs HAS RUN. The td ids
on a product page mean different grades than the ones on a listing page,
so a single read cannot be trusted. See data/top-graded-PLAN.md, trap 4.

excluded.name: Charizard [1st Edition] #4
excluded.public: its guide value moved between the two reads, so there are two correct readings of it and no basis for picking one
excluded.why: The market moved between the two reads, not a parse error. The listing crawl and the product page were both read 13 October 2026, hours apart, on the full price refresh. The product page carries its own dollar change from last update of +$2,606.00 on the Ungraded cell, and 12706 minus that change is 10100 exactly, which is the figure the listing crawl recorded. We hold two correctly read figures and no basis for calling either one the value, so the row is published nowhere until a later crawl reads it the same way twice.
excluded.systemic: verify-raw-top.mjs records the change and the reconciliation per column, and both disagreeing rows show reconciles: true on every column that disagrees; 158 of the 160 rows read identical on both page types. So the column mapping is right and these two cards moved.
